fields.h1: Build Hotel Automation Around Your Front Desk and Back Office

fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Hotel App
fields.features_subheading: Hotel automation hands the repeat steps of a stay to software and sends each exception to the person who owns it.
fields.feature_1:
Rules written the way you brief staff

Describe each rule in plain English, such as which room is cleaned first when an early guest waits. Emergent builds the app, its database, and the logic, and a prompt changes it.
fields.feature_2:
Connects to the systems the desk runs

The app connects to any tool with an API, so reservations come in from your property management system and updates go back out. QuickBooks and Stripe connect in the same way.
fields.feature_3:
Supplier invoices read into fields

Upload a linen or food supplier's invoice, and AI reads the vendor, the amount, and the due date into fields. A value the AI is unsure of goes to a person before the record is saved.
fields.feature_4:
A named owner for every exception

An unmatched charge or a low guest rating goes to one person by email or in the app, and a reminder follows if nobody acts. Slack alerts work the same way, set for each rule.
fields.feature_5:
No task cap in a sold-out week

Automations keep running with no task cap, so a full house with 60 arrivals runs the same rules as a quiet Tuesday. Guest, stay, and charge records sit in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
The code goes to your GitHub

Export the full code of the app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer the hotel trusts can read every rule before the app touches a guest folio or a card settlement.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Hotel Automations to Run This Month
fields.tab_content_1:
A late arrival checks in before she leaves home

Two days before her Larkhollow Hotel stay, Zuleika Varga-Mensah gets a check-in link with one question per screen. She gives an arrival time of 11:20 p.m. and signs the registration card. The app marks reservation R-40917 Checked in online and adds her to Caspian Mwangi-Roux's late-arrival list at the night desk.
fields.tab_content_2:
Room 312 goes first for a 1:00 p.m. guest

Room 312 checks out at 10:40 a.m. Manon Abernathy-Kalu asked to check in at 1:00 p.m. The app moves 312 to the top of the cleaning list for Perpetua Okonjo-Brandt in housekeeping. Perpetua marks the room Clean at 11:55 a.m., and the app emails Manon that her room is ready.
fields.tab_content_3:
A $186.40 charge with no settlement reaches the controller

At 3:00 a.m., the app sets the day's $14,382.50 in folio charges against the card settlement report. Of that, $14,196.10 matches. One $186.40 charge on room 118 has no settlement. Henrike Vantongeren, the controller, gets a Slack direct message with a Review button, and the matched total syncs to QuickBooks.
fields.tab_content_4:
Only guests who rate 4 or 5 get the rebooking offer

Two days after checkout, the app emails Agnieszka Ferrante-Obi a one-question survey. She rates her stay 2 of 5 and mentions street noise. The app leaves her off the $40 direct-booking offer, which only guests who rate 4 or 5 get, and emails her comment to Kwabena Asante-Holm, the general manager.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan hotel automation around a real booking and switch it on one flow at a time with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name the system that holds each fact
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write each rule as a sentence
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick one booking from last week and list each step a person did by hand for it: the check-in email, the room assignment, the card match, and the review request. Mark the steps that follow a fixed rule, and start with those.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down where each fact lives at your hotel: reservations in the property management system, settlements in the card processor's reports, revenue in the ledger. Connect each one through its API. Every automation should read a fact from the system that owns it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write each rule the way you would explain it to a new front desk hire. Send a parking pass link to guests who booked a space, and flag any group block with no rooming list 7 days before arrival. Emergent builds the app and its logic from those sentences.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide who hears about each exception before it happens: the controller for an unmatched charge, the general manager for a low rating, the night auditor for a no-show. Name a person rather than a channel, and set a reminder for when nobody acts.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Run last month's reservations and settlements through the app before it emails a single guest. Compare every flagged charge with what the controller found by hand, and check the order housekeeping would have cleaned in. Fix a rule by prompting, then run the same month again.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Switch on the night match first
fields.howto_step_6_des: Turn on charge matching first, because it never reaches a guest. Read every flagged charge for two weeks. Add online check-in next, then room turnover, and leave post-stay surveys for last, once the guest records are clean.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once a month, read everything a person had to fix by hand: charges matched manually, rooms cleaned out of order, ratings that missed the offer. Change the rule behind each repeat with a prompt, and check whether the list shrinks the next month.

faq_plan.a: Hotel automation hands the hotel work staff once did by hand to software that does it the same way every time. At an independent hotel, that means the repeat work around each stay: check-in links, cleaning order, the nightly card match, and post-stay emails.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up hotel automation?
faq_plan.a: Pick one rule the front desk follows the same way every time and describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder, which turns it into a working app. Connect the property management system through its API, test the rule on past bookings, and switch it on once every result checks out.

faq_plan.q: What should automated hotel accounting software verify every night?
faq_plan.a: It should check that every folio charge has a matching card settlement, that the day's revenue lands in the right ledger accounts, and that direct-bill balances sit on the right company account. Anything that fails a check needs a named person to clear it. An app built on Emergent keeps those records in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can automated hotel check in handle corporate guests on direct billing?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the check-in flow asks for the company name and checks it against the accounts approved for direct billing. A match skips the card step, and at checkout the folio becomes an invoice to that company. From there, accounts receivable automation tracks the invoice until it is paid.

faq_plan.q: What should hotel automation software connect to first?
faq_plan.a: Connect it to the property management system first, because every booking and room assignment at the front desk starts there. Add the card processor and the accounting ledger next. Apps built on Emergent can sync data in and out of each one through its API.

faq_plan.q: What front desk work should hotel automation solutions leave to people?
faq_plan.a: Leave the conversations a guest remembers to people: a late arrival who needs directions, or a complaint at the desk. Hand software the repeat steps, such as sending check-in links or matching charges, and name the person who handles each exception.

faq_plan.q: Which back-office tasks should hotel automation take on after check-in?
faq_plan.a: Supplier invoices come next. Linen and food bills arrive on a steady schedule. An app can read each one into fields and route it for approval before payment, which is the core of accounts payable automation. Start with the supplier that sends the most invoices each month.

faq_plan.q: Should automated hotel payment processing store guest card numbers?
faq_plan.a: No. Let the card processor hold card numbers, and have the app store only the processor's reference, the amount, and the room. Any system that keeps or handles card data falls under PCI DSS. Check with your processor before the app touches a card number at all.

faq_plan.q: What should marketing automation for hotels send after a stay?
faq_plan.a: Start with a post-stay survey and a rebooking offer. Then add emails timed to each guest's own history: a note a month before the dates of last year's stay, or a parking reminder for guests who drove. Tie every list to the guest record. That way nobody gets a promotion the week after a complaint.

faq_plan.q: Can hotel automation technology run the same rules at several properties?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Write each rule once with a property field. The same card match then runs at every hotel, and each property's exceptions go to its own controller. Roll every property's revenue into one set of books with accounting automation. Automations built on Emergent have no task cap as properties are added.

plan.angle: The top 10 are property management and hospitality vendors (NetSuite, SiteMinder, Cloudbeds, Oracle, Mews, Canary) plus a robotics blog, each listing the benefits of automating a hotel in general terms. None shows a working automation an independent hotel can run next week. This page shows four at one 60-room independent hotel, the Larkhollow Hotel, as working screens: an online check-in for a late arrival, a room cleaned first for an early guest, a nightly match of folio charges against card settlements, and a post-stay survey that decides who gets a rebooking offer. The FAQ covers accounting, check-in, payments and marketing questions a hotel operator asks, with sources.
